description: Two-panel composite figure of scanning electron micrographs showing inclusion morphologies in a light grey steel matrix; both panels carry a "2 µm" scale bar in the lower left and are labelled "(a)" and "(b)". (a) shows a single dark, polyhedral inclusion with straight edges and sharp angles embedded in the matrix; the particle is roughly equiaxed with a bright halo at its interface with the matrix, and faint straight line features (polishing scratches or slip traces) cross the surrounding matrix. (b) shows a dark inclusion body that is clearly fragmented — several angular sub-particles with straight edges and sharp corners grouped in a compact cluster, with thin matrix-like gaps separating the fragments, consistent with a particle that has been broken. Neither panel contains an EDS spectrum, elemental map or diffraction pattern, so the phase identity is not confirmed by the pixels themselves; the caption attributes both morphologies to AlN inclusions in HN steel. Taken together the two panels demonstrate that the AlN inclusions of HN steel are faceted, polyhedral and angular with straight edges and sharp angles, and that an individual inclusion can be fractured into several fragments — the feature the citing text links to forging and to crack initiation.

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains a single dark, faceted inclusion with straight edges and sharp angles set in a light grey matrix.
Panel (b) shows a dark inclusion body broken into a cluster of several angular fragments with straight edges and sharp corners, separated by thin gaps.
Both panels carry a scale bar labelled "2 µm" in the lower left corner.
A bright halo surrounds the inclusion/matrix interface in both panels, and faint straight line features (scratches or slip traces) cross the matrix.
Neither panel includes an EDS spectrum, elemental map or diffraction pattern, so the inclusion phase is not identified by the image pixels themselves.
The caption states the figure shows typical morphologies of AlN inclusions in HN steel.
The citing text states that for the HN steel the main inclusion is AlN with a straight edge and sharp angle.
The citing text states that AlN inclusions could be broken after forging, as shown in Figure 5b, and generally became the crack origin of the steel fracture.

The citing text describes the LN steel as instead containing AlN, Mn(Mg)S and their composite inclusions, with elliptical, smooth-edged sulfide inclusions, contrasting with the angular AlN morphology in this figure.

The citing text notes that AlN is generated during solidification with lower Al and N contents and can form in molten steel with higher Al and N contents, and that AlN becomes dominant as N content increases.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph with a 2 µm scale bar showing one dark, roughly equiaxed polyhedral inclusion with straight edges and sharp angles in a light grey matrix; a bright halo surrounds the particle/matrix interface and faint straight scratches or slip traces cross the matrix.

SEM micrograph with a 2 µm scale bar showing a dark inclusion that is broken into a cluster of several angular fragments with straight edges and sharp corners, separated by narrow matrix-filled gaps, consistent with a fractured inclusion.

unreadable_items: No numeric particle-size values are printed in either panel; inclusion dimensions can only be judged relative to the 2 µm scale bars.
Inclusion phase (AlN) is not confirmed by any in-figure spectroscopy or diffraction — it is asserted only in the caption.
